@SYChen123 Thanks for the invitation to collaborate. I put runnable reproductions in https://github.com/SuperGoodGame/sglang/pull/1, based directly on your current head `fd6cf87` (no production changes).

I observed four things:

1. **Submission after a failed sub-batch.** With four requests split into two pairs and the first transport call returning -1, batching still submits the second pair to the same session. Disabled/enabled batching makes 1/2 calls respectively; `failed_sessions` is still empty at the second call. All requests ultimately become Failed; I did not observe false success or data corruption. Could we stop further submissions to that session immediately, while preserving deferred-release poisoning and failing unsubmitted members?

2. **Repeated planning on singleton fallback.** With eight requests and a byte cap that only fits one request, both modes make eight submissions, but layer planning runs 8 times with batching disabled versus 16 when enabled. The prepared singleton plan is discarded and rebuilt by the fallback. Reusing that plan, or avoiding futile preplanning, may help.

3. **Completion waits across bounded sub-batches.** At the start of request 3's transfer, requests 1–2 are already Success without batching, but neither is Success with batching. Both modes finish correctly. This is a latency tradeoff: could each completed bounded sub-batch publish its per-request completion before blocking on later sub-batches, subject to state/aux, cancellation and lifetime constraints?

4. **Adjacent ranges are concatenated rather than coalesced.** Two requests with separate K/V buffers submit 4 descriptors even when both source and destination pages are contiguous. An offline candidate uses 2 descriptors and produces identical destination buffers. Source-only or destination-only adjacency correctly leaves 4. Coalescing within compatible layer/buffer groups only when **both** ends are adjacent looks worth exploring; its speedup has not been measured.

These are CPU-copy reproductions exercising the real planner/worker, not GPU performance benchmarks. The [README](https://github.com/SuperGoodGame/sglang/blob/repro/mooncake-descriptor-coalescing/test/manual/disaggregation/README.mooncake-batching.md) has commands and expected results; both scripts and the existing 13 batching tests pass locally.

Could you try reproducing these? The [single commit](https://github.com/SuperGoodGame/sglang/commit/0c79c5403ab984d0cd74446b94cad1f148106a21) can be cherry-picked onto this branch.

Hi @SYChen123, we’ve been working on incremental improvements to the fragmented equal-TP KV staging implementation in #35036, with our changes submitted to its author’s branch: https://github.com/KIOSHIROI/sglang/pull/1.

One potential integration with this PR would be:

1. Select the transfer path per chunk based on staging eligibility and fragmentation.
2. Route eligible fragmented chunks through staging.
3. Allow eligible direct-transfer chunks to participate in cross-request batching even when staging is enabled.

This integration is not implemented yet. Would you be interested in working together on it? We can contribute the staging-side changes and coordinate with you on the batching integration.

@simple-sun Hi, thanks for your information. This current PR doesn't consider staging. To adapt staging into cross-req batching, we should avoid different requests' staging buffers being reused and mixed. This will probably introduce much complexity and it's out of the scope of this PR. I think I need to first demonstrate the performance of cross-req batching. If it's truly beneficial, then we can integrate other features step by step.

+        # Tracing keeps the legacy path so request spans include the actual IO.

+                or self.custom_mem_pool_type == "INTRA_NODE_NVLINK"

+            and type(self).send_kvcache is MooncakeKVManager.send_kvcache
+            and type(self)._send_kvcache_generic

+    def _plan_request_batch_chunk(
+        self, chunk: TransferKVChunk
+    ) -> Optional[List[_RequestBatchTransfer]]:
+        """Build direct-write descriptors without sending or publishing success.
+
+        Returning None creates a FIFO barrier: this and subsequent chunks use
+        the legacy worker path, including event waits, relayout and staging.
+        """
+        if (
+            chunk.wait_event is not None
+            or self.request_status.get(chunk.room)
+            not in (KVPoll.WaitingForInput, KVPoll.Transferring)
+            or not chunk.prefill_kv_indices.size
+            or not self.kv_args.kv_data_ptrs
+        ):
+            return None
+        transfers = []
+        for req in list(self.transfer_infos.get(chunk.room, {}).values()):
+            if req.is_dummy:
+                continue
+            with self.session_lock:
+                if (
+                    req.mooncake_session_id in self.failed_sessions
+                    or req.mooncake_session_id in self.state_layout_rejections
+                ):
+                    return None
+                peer = self.decode_kv_args_table[req.mooncake_session_id]
+            if (
+                peer.requires_dcp_relayout
+                or req.dst_device_kv_indices is not None
+                or not (
+                    self.is_mla_backend
+                    or self.is_hybrid_mla_backend
+                    or self.attn_tp_size == peer.dst_attn_tp_size
+                )
+                or self._get_dsa_cache_transfer_skip_flags(peer)[0]
+            ):
+                return None
+            dst_indices = req.dst_kv_indices[chunk.index_slice]
+            if dst_indices.size != chunk.prefill_kv_indices.size:
+                # Preserve the existing page-tail workaround on the legacy path.
+                return None
+            self._validate_envelope_kv_layout(
+                peer.dst_kv_ptrs, peer.dst_kv_item_len, peer.dst_attn_tp_size
+            )
+            layers = self._get_kvcache_layer_params(
+                self.kv_args.kv_data_ptrs,
+                peer.dst_kv_ptrs,
+                self.kv_args.kv_item_lens,
+                force_flat=get_memory().enable_unified_memory,
+                src_layer_ids=self.kv_args.kv_layer_ids,
+                dst_layer_ids=peer.dst_kv_layer_ids,
+            )
+            if layers is None:
+                return None
+            src_ranges, dst_ranges = group_concurrent_contiguous(
+                chunk.prefill_kv_indices, dst_indices
+            )
+            num_bytes = chunk.prefill_kv_indices.size * sum(
+                item_len for _, _, item_len in layers
+            )
+            if (
+                len(layers) * len(src_ranges) > self.max_request_batch_descriptors
+                or num_bytes > self.max_request_batch_bytes
+            ):
+                # Do not construct an oversized list just to discard it later.
+                return None
+            blocks = [
+                (
+                    src_ptr + int(src_range[0]) * item_len,
+                    dst_ptr + int(dst_range[0]) * item_len,
+                    len(src_range) * item_len,
+                )
+                for src_ptr, dst_ptr, item_len in layers
+                for src_range, dst_range in zip(src_ranges, dst_ranges)
+            ]
+            transfers.append((chunk, req, blocks))
+        return transfers or None
+
+    def _send_request_batch(
+        self, chunks: Collection[TransferKVChunk]
+    ) -> Dict[Tuple[int, str], int]:
+        """Send bounded, same-session groups and retain a result per chunk/peer.
+
+        Only a prefix of distinct rooms with the same destination-session set
+        is planned. A second chunk of the same room is a barrier, preserving
+        its KV/state/aux ordering. Singleton and oversized groups fall back to
+        the original per-request submission.
+        """
+        if len(chunks) < 2:
+            return {}
+        groups: Dict[str, List[_RequestBatchTransfer]] = defaultdict(list)
+        rooms = set()
+        sessions = None
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            if chunk.room in rooms:
+                break
+            transfers = self._plan_request_batch_chunk(chunk)
+            if transfers is None:
+                break
+            chunk_sessions = {req.mooncake_session_id for _, req, _ in transfers}
+            if sessions is not None and chunk_sessions != sessions:
+                # Complete the earlier cohort before blocking on a different
+                # decode pool that happens to hash to the same queue.
+                break
+            sessions = chunk_sessions
+            rooms.add(chunk.room)
+            for transfer in transfers:
+                groups[transfer[1].mooncake_session_id].append(transfer)
+
+        results = {}
+
+        def submit(session, members):
+            # An abort may have arrived while addresses were being planned.
+            members = [
+                member
+                for member in members
+                if self.request_status.get(member[0].room, KVPoll.Failed)
+                != KVPoll.Failed
+            ]
+            if len(members) < 2:
+                return
+            blocks = [block for _, _, plan in members for block in plan]
+            ret = self._transfer_data(session, blocks)
+            for chunk, _, _ in members:
+                results[(id(chunk), session)] = ret
+                if ret != 0:
+                    # A failed/timeout batch does not prove every write drained.
+                    # Keep decode's deferred-release ACK conservative.
+                    self.poison_deferred_ack_room(chunk.room)
+
+        for session, transfers in groups.items():
+            members = []

@SYChen123 Thanks for the invitation to collaborate. I put runnable reproductions in https://github.com/SuperGoodGame/sglang/pull/1, based directly on your current head `fd6cf87` (no production changes).

I observed four things:

1. **Submission after a failed sub-batch.** With four requests split into two pairs and the first transport call returning -1, batching still submits the second pair to the same session. Disabled/enabled batching makes 1/2 calls respectively; `failed_sessions` is still empty at the second call. All requests ultimately become Failed; I did not observe false success or data corruption. Could we stop further submissions to that session immediately, while preserving deferred-release poisoning and failing unsubmitted members?

2. **Repeated planning on singleton fallback.** With eight requests and a byte cap that only fits one request, both modes make eight submissions, but layer planning runs 8 times with batching disabled versus 16 when enabled. The prepared singleton plan is discarded and rebuilt by the fallback. Reusing that plan, or avoiding futile preplanning, may help.

3. **Completion waits across bounded sub-batches.** At the start of request 3's transfer, requests 1–2 are already Success without batching, but neither is Success with batching. Both modes finish correctly. This is a latency tradeoff: could each completed bounded sub-batch publish its per-request completion before blocking on later sub-batches, subject to state/aux, cancellation and lifetime constraints?

4. **Adjacent ranges are concatenated rather than coalesced.** Two requests with separate K/V buffers submit 4 descriptors even when both source and destination pages are contiguous. An offline candidate uses 2 descriptors and produces identical destination buffers. Source-only or destination-only adjacency correctly leaves 4. Coalescing within compatible layer/buffer groups only when **both** ends are adjacent looks worth exploring; its speedup has not been measured.

These are CPU-copy reproductions exercising the real planner/worker, not GPU performance benchmarks. The [README](https://github.com/SuperGoodGame/sglang/blob/repro/mooncake-descriptor-coalescing/test/manual/disaggregation/README.mooncake-batching.md) has commands and expected results; both scripts and the existing 13 batching tests pass locally.

Could you try reproducing these? The [single commit](https://github.com/SuperGoodGame/sglang/commit/0c79c5403ab984d0cd74446b94cad1f148106a21) can be cherry-picked onto this branch.

Hi @SYChen123, we’ve been working on incremental improvements to the fragmented equal-TP KV staging implementation in #35036, with our changes submitted to its author’s branch: https://github.com/KIOSHIROI/sglang/pull/1.

One potential integration with this PR would be:

1. Select the transfer path per chunk based on staging eligibility and fragmentation.
2. Route eligible fragmented chunks through staging.
3. Allow eligible direct-transfer chunks to participate in cross-request batching even when staging is enabled.

This integration is not implemented yet. Would you be interested in working together on it? We can contribute the staging-side changes and coordinate with you on the batching integration.

@simple-sun Hi, thanks for your information. This current PR doesn't consider staging. To adapt staging into cross-req batching, we should avoid different requests' staging buffers being reused and mixed. This will probably introduce much complexity and it's out of the scope of this PR. I think I need to first demonstrate the performance of cross-req batching. If it's truly beneficial, then we can integrate other features step by step.
